text.p: Blue-chip stocks egded higher Monday as strength in oil stocks counterbalanced profit-taking after last week's history-setting advance.
At 1 p.m. EDT, the Dow Jones industrial index was up 0.40 of a point at 6,703.95.
Investors called time out in the blue-chip market after boosting the Dow index last week by 312 points, its biggest weekly gain ever on upbeat corporate earnings.
In the broader market, declining issues led advances 6-5 on trading of more than 205 million shares on the New York Stock Exchange.
The Nasdaq Composite index was off 3.83 points at 1,218.74.
Better-than-expected first quarter results from Dow component Exxon Corp. provided the spark for the stocks of oil companies.
"The numbers on Exxon were good, so the oils are a little better," said Robert Stovall, president of Stovall Twenty-First Advisers.
Exxon was up 1-3/8 to 54-7/8 and Chevron Corp., another Dow component, rose 1-1/4 to 65-7/8.
For the broader market, however, Stovall added, "there's no real catalyst or spark today."
James Volk, director of equity trading at Jensen Securities, said, "The market has gone too far, too fast and has gotten ahead of itself and should probably back off from here."
Technology stocks, particularily in the computer networking and storage groups, backed off despite further gains by market heavyweight Microsoft Corp.

After rising 9-1/2 Friday on better-than-expected quarterly earnings, Microsoft added 2-7/16 to 110-1/16 on Monday. But Ascend Communications Inc. fell 1-1/4 to 39, Qualcomm Inc. lost 1-1/2 to 46-3/4 and Western Digital Corp. was off 1-3/8 to 59-3/8.
Analysts said the divergence amid technology stocks was a sign of investors becoming increasingly picky about the stocks they were willing to buy.
"It's getting much, much more selective, and I think that's an indicator of a late bull market cycle," said Bruce Bittles, market strategist at J.C. Bradford.
Among the active stocks, Gould Pumps Inc. soared 13-1/4 to 36-1/8 after ITT Industries Inc. agreed to acquire the company for $37 per share plus assumption of debt. ITT Industries rose 1/4 to 23-5/8.
